Enquiries with budget fit, replies and follow-ups
One row per enquiry: contact, project type, source, budget and rooms; the budget fit by tier, reply and proposal timing, follow-up checks and the value of a won project fill in by themselves.
Proposals with fee share, expiry and chase check
One row per proposal sent: fee type, fee estimate, FF&E budget, expiry and status; the fee share of the budget, days to expiry, who to chase and the signing time fill in by themselves.
Proposal lines priced from the rate card
One row per service line of a proposal: service, quantity and rate; the unit, line total and share of the proposal fill in by themselves.
Rate card of design services with cost and margin
One row per service the studio sells: unit, who does it, rate and minimum units; the cost of the unit at your hour cost, the margin and the smallest charge fill in by themselves.
Fixed, hourly and percentage fee side by side
Twelve sample projects with the FF&E budget, hours and fixed fee; the hourly and percentage fees, the studio income per hour of each model and the best model fill in by themselves.
First meetings with outcome and days to proposal
One row per first meeting: enquiry, kind, minutes, designer and outcome; the contact, phone, days until the proposal and the next-step check fill in by themselves.
Design briefs with budget per room and deadline
One row per design brief: rooms, budget, deadline, decision makers, must-haves and style in plain words; the contact, budget per room and the weeks to the deadline fill in by themselves.
Projects with fee type, fee share and value per sqm
One row per project: client, type, fee type, fee, FF&E budget, lead and status; the fee share of the FF&E budget and the value per sqm fill in by themselves.
Fee share of the FF&E budget
Clients with projects, value and repeat flag
One row per client or prospect: kind, contact, terms, source and stage; the number of projects, total contract value and the repeat client flag fill in by themselves.
Referral partners with leads, bookings and value
One row per architect, builder, showroom contact, agent, maker or past client who sends work; the leads, bookings, value won and a thank-you reminder fill in from the enquiries.
Marketing results with cost per enquiry and per project
One row per month and source: spend, enquiries, bookings and revenue; the cost per enquiry, cost per booking and revenue per unit spent fill in by themselves.
Follow-up log with days since the last touch
One row per contact with a prospect: the enquiry or proposal, date, channel and outcome; the contact, days since this touch and since the latest touch fill in by themselves.
Lost enquiries with reason, price gap and lesson
One row per enquiry or proposal that did not become a project: reason, price gap, who won and what would have saved it; the contact, budget and gap share fill in by themselves.
Packages with fee model and price per room
Twelve ready packages by project type: rooms, fee model, price and what is included; the price per room fills in by itself.
FF&E allowance per room by tier
The FF&E allowance for each room type at three tiers with typical size and items; the allowance per sqm fills in by itself and feeds the budget fit of every enquiry.
Proposal terms library with review dates
Twelve standard clauses for proposals with the days, rounds or share they use and the date each is reviewed; the days to review and a review check fill in by themselves.
Retainers with due date, days to pay and state
One row per retainer invoice: project, amount, dates and what it is credited against; the client, phone, days to pay and whether it is paid, late or overdue fill in by themselves.
Design capacity by week with free hours
One row per week: designers working and hours already committed from active projects; the hours available, free hours, utilisation and whether a new project fits fill in by themselves.
Team with roles, hour cost, bill rate and booked until
The owner designer, four staff and seven freelance specialists: role, hours a week, hour cost and bill rate; the margin per hour and the weeks booked ahead fill in by themselves.
Pipeline by month with win rate
One row per month: enquiries, proposals, projects won and lost and the value won; the win rate of decided proposals and the average value per project fill in by themselves.

Type the rooms, tier, sqm and trades budget; the FF&E budget comes from your room allowances; see the fee, reserve, total price, price per sqm and margin before labour.

Hello {contact}, thank you for your enquiry about your {project_type} project. Can we talk on {follow_up_date}? Please tell me a time that suits you.
Hello {contact}, your {kind} with {designer} is confirmed for {date}, about {minutes} minutes. Please tell us if the time changes.
Hello {contact}, to prepare for our meeting please send room measurements, photos of each room and any plans you have for your {project_type} project.
Client: your design brief is ready
Hello {contact}, your design brief for {rooms} rooms is ready. The budget is {budget}, which is {budget_room} per room. Please check it and tell us what to change.
Hello {contact}, your proposal for the {project_type} project is ready. The design fee estimate is {fee_estimate} ({fee_type}). Shall we go through it together?
Client: your proposal is valid until
Hello {contact}, your proposal is valid until {valid_until}. After that the fee and the start date may change. Please tell us if you need more time.
Hello {contact}, a gentle reminder about the proposal we sent on {date_sent}. Do you have questions, or would a call help?
Hello {contact}, for your budget of {budget_est} we can offer three levels of FF&E: Essential {opt_ess}, Refined {opt_ref} or Luxury {opt_lux}. Which feels closest?
Hello {contact}, you asked for a {fee_type} fee. We can also work with a fixed fee, an hourly fee or a percentage of the FF&E spend. I will send a short page that explains each one.
Client: your retainer secures the date
Hello {client}, the retainer of {amount} secures your start date. It is due on {due_date} and is credited against your first fee invoice.
Hello {client}, your retainer of {amount} arrived on {paid_on}. Welcome. We will confirm your start date and the kick-off meeting.
Hello {contact}, thank you for signing. Next steps: the retainer, the kick-off meeting and the room measurements. Your project number is {project_id}.
Client: we cannot start before this date
Hello {contact}, we cannot start before {earliest_start} because our design team is full until then. Is that date fine for you?
Client: sorry we could not take it
Hello {contact}, thank you for considering us. We are sorry we could not take your project. We would be glad to help in the future.
Client: thank you for the referral
Hello {contact}, thank you for recommending us to a friend. It means a great deal to the whole studio.
Client: your proposal change is attached
